h: The House of Hashem and the Stream of Shabbos Delight

p: there is mentioned in the zemiros
and at the second meal we say,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יג)
"And you shall call Shabbos a delight";
and it is stated in the holy Zohar
and they are the holiness of
"And a river goes forth from Eden
"How precious is Your kindness, God, etc.;
they shall be sated with the abundance of Your house,
and You give them drink from the stream of Your delights";
when they are sated with the abundance of the house of Hashem,
then "You give them drink from the stream of Your delights":
if the pasuk "the abundance of Your house"
after all, it is permitted to enter
that I may dwell in the house of Hashem
all the days of my life";
yet in the time of David HaMelech,
the House had not yet been built,
and there was only a bamah;
what they said in the Gemara
and batei midrash in Bavel, etc.
What is it that is written (Tehillim 90:1):
'Hashem, You have been a dwelling place for us'?
ה׳ אָהַבְתִּי מְעוֹן בֵּיתֶךָ (שָׁם כו, ח)
'Hashem, I love the dwelling place of Your house' (ibid. 26:8)
only the four cubits of halachah."
And this is like the dispute
whether the holiness of the beis knesses is greater
or the holiness of the beis midrash is greater;
both are called the house of Hashem,
for he is the root of prayer;
is like standing before the King;
we call it Torah she'b'al peh.
of those possessed of ruach hakodesh;
is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
"A sage is greater than a prophet,"
the root of Torah and prayer;
"that I may dwell in the house of Hashem
all the days of my life."
And this is what it says:
"How precious is Your kindness, God, etc.;
they shall be sated with the abundance of Your house":
for this one needs the kindness of Hashem,
as they said in the Gemara
to be a vessel for Torah."
And one needs merit to merit this;
בְּזֵעַת אַפְּךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, יט)
"By the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread" (Bereishis 3:19).
And one needs merit to merit this:
as is written in the holy Zohar.
"Shabbos is to be made entirely Torah";
that he makes it entirely Torah.
are called dwellers in the house of Hashem,
"You who dwell in the gardens" (Shir HaShirim 8:13)
that although they are occupied with their work
and at the time of the meals,
who keep the three meals, are called
as is written in the holy Zohar
and there is fulfilled in them
"they shall be sated with the abundance of Your house,
and You give them drink from the stream of Your delights,"
as though dwelling in Gan Eden;
as is expounded in the Gemara
the fragrance of a field of apples";
and then "You give them drink from the stream of Your delights."
take refuge in the shadow of Your wings,"
"But one who takes refuge in Me
that he will possess the Beis HaMikdash?
of the matter of blemishing the covenant
"The face of Hashem is against evildoers";
as is explained in the holy Zohar
for crying out helps for this.
and those who hate the tzaddik will be condemned" (ibid. 34:22):
that is, only those who hate
the attribute of "Tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
to make the effort to rectify it.
like a servant before the King
Since it is written "and none shall be condemned,"
it implies that they were deserving
for they were corrupted in this;
"But one who takes refuge in Me shall inherit the land";
forever they shall inherit the land"
have a share in the World to Come,
which will become clear in the future,
that he will merit to be
dwelling in the house of Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא בֵּיתִי בֵּית תְּפִלָּה (שָׁם נו, ז)
which is "My house, a house of prayer" (ibid. 56:7);
that the beis knesses is called "dwelling place."
because there was written about him,
in the matter of this blemish,
"And I have done what is evil in Your eyes"
"that I may dwell in the house of Hashem
all the days of my life,"
for he was the root of prayer;
"In You, Hashem, I have taken refuge,"
"Let me not be shamed, for I have taken refuge in You."
And this is what it says:
take refuge in the shadow of Your wings";
and one who takes refuge in Hashem
"they shall be sated with the abundance of Your house,
and You give them drink from the stream of Your delights,"
